title: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Attention for Cooperative and Scalable Feature Transformation

problem.claim: Feature transformation is important for structured-data tasks because deep models may not capture complex feature interactions effectively.

gap.claim: Existing automated approaches can be inefficient or time-consuming, while reinforcement-learning approaches remain limited by instability and time complexity from dynamic feature expansion and insufficient agent cooperation and communication.

contributions.claim: A heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement-learning framework for cooperative and scalable feature transformation, comprising three heterogeneous agents grouped into two types to select features and operations for feature crossing.
A shared critic mechanism for information exchange among agents during feature transformation.
Multi-head attention-based feature agents for dynamic feature-space selection, together with state encoding to stabilize reinforcement-learning optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present a novel heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement-learning framework for cooperative and scalable feature transformation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments intended to validate the model's effectiveness, efficiency, robustness, and interpretability.
The authors report that the code and dataset are publicly available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Feature transformation generates informative features through mathematical feature crossing and remains important for structured data.
Existing automated methods often use heuristics or exhaustive search, while recent reinforcement-learning methods use trial-and-error to improve traditional approaches.
Dynamic feature expansion and weak cooperation or communication among agents create instability, higher learning complexity, and suboptimal feature crossing.
The proposed framework uses heterogeneous agents, a shared critic, multi-head attention for feature selection, and state encoding for more stable learning.
The authors report extensive experiments and public release of the code and dataset.

source_observation.claim: Dynamic feature expansion can destabilize reinforcement-learning feature transformation and increase learning time complexity.

interpretation.claim: A changing action or feature space may require representations and selection mechanisms that preserve global context while controlling learning instability.

application.claim: For reinforcement-learning systems with expanding feature spaces, consider attention-based selection and explicit state encoding.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these mechanisms generalize beyond the reported feature-transformation setting.

source_observation.claim: Insufficient cooperation and communication between agents can produce suboptimal feature-crossing operations and degraded model performance.

interpretation.claim: Multi-agent systems may benefit from shared information pathways when agents make interdependent decisions.

application.claim: Use a shared critic or comparable coordination mechanism when heterogeneous agents must jointly select interacting operations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when shared communication may introduce interference or overhead.

unknowns: The abstract does not report datasets, task definitions, baselines, quantitative results, or statistical evaluation details.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, or the scope of the claimed interpretability.
The abstract does not describe the public repository location beyond stating that it is on GitHub.
